fields.v: Jiang, Z., Wang, R., Hu, Y., Wang, Y., Jia, Y., Gong, N. Z. (2026). Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.00650v1 [cs.CL], 30 Sep 2026

Conference — NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems), per the camera-ready footer on p. 1; full text read from arXiv:2610.00650v1 [cs.CL]; acceptance not confirmed from another source
fields.why: Only evidence of the venue is the NeurIPS 2026 camera-ready footer on p. 1 of the arXiv copy (no DOI, no proceedings reference). Author to confirm acceptance; if not accepted, Preprint

fields.v: Duke University (all six authors)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — RuleEvolve, self-evolving framework for coding rules (AGENTS.md / system prompt), compared with no rule, a manual rule and Prompt-Ops across 2 agent frameworks, 4 backbone models, 3 benchmarks plus SWE-bench Lite

RuleEvolve (no version): pool of m candidate coding rules evolved by an LLM mutator and a judge module, with strategic mutation allocation based on Optimal Computing Budget Allocation (OCBA). Baselines: No rule; Manual rule (from awesome-cursorrules repository, App. F); Prompt-Ops (LLM prompt duel optimizer, default settings); ablations: even and proportional allocation

Coding rules file (AGENTS.md for OpenHands; system prompt for OpenAI SDK agent). Evolved rule has 16 sections in six categories (output format/self-containment, algorithm knowledge, brevity style, API/library idiom, correctness tactics, process/budget)

Initial rules -> mutator generates m variants -> judge runs agent on mini-batch of training tasks and scores (code characters + lambda x correctness penalty vs no-rule) -> allocate N mutations by OCBA -> evaluate -> prune to top m -> repeat T iterations -> return best rule
None (automatic loop); only the initial rule is human-written
Single artefact (coding rules / context file), evolved and then used by the agent
Not classifiable (coding rules / AGENTS.md, no specification)
Mostly function-level code generation from a problem description (BigCodeBench, BigCodeBench-Hard, HumanEval); existing code base only in SWE-Bench Lite (repository-level issues)

Training: 1,000 random BigCodeBench instances (mini-batches of B = 10); testing: 100 random samples each of BCB (disjoint), BCB-Hard, HumanEval; SWE-Bench Lite 100-task subset. Parameters T = 10, N = 20, m = 5, lambda = 3,000
Python programming tasks (general, library function calls); SWE-Bench Lite Python repositories
N/A (no human participants)
Average generation time (s); average token usage (computed only on functionally correct code). Cost of the evolution process itself not reported
Pass rate (share of generated code passing all test cases); Pass@k (k = 1-10)

Average code lines and code characters (main); App. D: duplicated-block ratio, cyclomatic complexity, Halstead volume, maintainability index, complexity per SLOC, docstring rate (No rule vs RuleEvolve only)
Not measured
Character attribution per rule category (ablation of rule sections, App. C)
Automatic: benchmark test cases, token counts, generation time, code metrics

Criterion: pass rate on 100-sample test sets; values PR BCB/BCB-H/HE; tokens BCB (Tables 5-6); rules evolved per backbone. OpenHands (rules via AGENTS.md): - gpt-4.1-mini: No rule 0.48/0.27/0.96, 1079; Manual 0.48/0.28/0.95, 1320; Prompt-Ops 0.43/0.22/0.71, 903.1; RuleEvolve 0.50/0.28/0.98, 991.6. - gpt-5-mini: No rule 0.40/0.18/0.97, 1793; Manual 0.38/0.22/0.96, 2047; Prompt-Ops 0.33/0.19/0.99, 1392; RuleEvolve 0.41/0.25/0.98, 1498. - gpt-5.3-codex: No rule 0.49/0.29/0.99, 1143; Manual 0.49/0.29/0.99, 1293; Prompt-Ops 0.40/0.25/0.91, 1009; RuleEvolve 0.52/0.27/0.99, 1016. - Qwen-Coder-30B: No rule 0.43/0.27/0.97, 1250; Manual 0.44/0.28/0.99, 1262; Prompt-Ops 0.35/0.19/0.91, 1119; RuleEvolve 0.44/0.27/0.96, 1028. Verdicts, each configuration on its own: RuleEvolve (all 8 framework-model cells): quality partly (BCB 0.38-0.52, BCB-H 0.19-0.28, HE 0.88-0.99); cost works (about 480-1,720 tokens and 3-23 s per task; cost of the evolution runs not reported). No rule (all 8): quality partly (BCB 0.17-0.49, BCB-H 0.12-0.29, HE 0.90-0.99); cost works. Manual rule (all 8): quality partly (HE falls to 0.68-0.69 with SDK gpt-5-mini and Qwen); cost works (highest or near-highest tokens, up to 2,799). Prompt-Ops (all 8): quality partly (BCB 0.32-0.48, HE down to 0.67); cost works. Multi-seed (gpt-4.1-mini, BCB, 10 seeds; framework not stated): No rule PR 0.502 +/- 0.015, 1181 tok, 8.66 s; Public rule 0.498, 2049; Prompt-Ops 0.502, 1130; RuleEvolve 0.502 +/- 0.026, 1019 tok, 9.67 s; all four quality partly (PR about 0.50), cost works. SWE-Bench Lite (gpt-4.1-mini, framework not stated): No rule PR 0.330, 131.17 s, 911 tok (quality partly; cost works); Public rule 0.190, 166.45 s, 867 tok (quality does not work; cost works); Prompt-Ops 0.080, 175.24 s, 684 tok (quality does not work; cost works); RuleEvolve 0.340, 297.46 s, 722 tok (quality partly; cost partly, time more than double No rule). Ablation (mutation allocation; backbone, framework and benchmark not stated for Fig. 2b): even, proportional, OCBA all PR 0.500; tokens 980.9 / 998.6 / 975.2; time 20.47 / 17.37 / 15.48 s (value labels in Fig. 2b)
fields.why: Multi-seed entry was attributed to the OpenAI SDK, but p. 7 and Table 3 name only the backbone and benchmark (the No rule values, 1181 tokens and 8.66 s, are closer to the OpenHands than to the SDK single run); the ablation entry's setting (gpt-4.1-mini, BCB) is not stated for Fig. 2b. Numbers re-checked against Tables 3-6 and Fig. 2b; verdict levels remain a judgement

fields.v: Tasks: 100-sample test sets of BCB, BCB-Hard, HumanEval; SWE-Bench Lite 100 tasks. Configurations: 4 methods x 2 frameworks (OpenAI SDK custom agent, OpenHands) x 4 backbones; rules evolved per model. Baselines: No rule, Manual rule, Prompt-Ops; ablation: even/proportional allocation, T, N, m. Held constant: framework, backbone, test samples within comparison. Acceptance tests: benchmark test cases. Repetitions: single run per cell in main tables; 10 seeds for the four methods in one setting (gpt-4.1-mini, BCB, framework not stated). Human intervention: none. Mutator LLM not stated
fields.why: The 10-seed run (Table 3) covers all four methods (No rule, Public rule, Prompt-Ops, RuleEvolve), not one configuration, and its framework is not stated

fields.v: RuleEvolve reaches highest or near-highest PR and lower code length/tokens than No rule and Manual rule in most cells, e.g. OpenAI SDK gpt-5.3-codex BCB PR 0.49 vs 0.45 manual, chars 453.1 vs 2372, tokens 544.5 vs 1022; gpt-5-mini BCB 0.46 vs 0.31 manual, ~40% fewer tokens (1717 vs 2799). Prompt-Ops sometimes cheaper but drops PR (same backbone, OpenHands gpt-5.3-codex BCB 0.40 vs 0.52; the paper's 0.43 vs 0.52 compares Prompt-Ops on gpt-4.1-mini with RuleEvolve on gpt-5.3-codex). Multi-seed: PR equal (0.502) with fewer lines (24.3 vs 32.5) and tokens (1019 vs 1181), but time higher (9.67 vs 8.66 s). SWE-Bench Lite: 0.340 vs 0.330 no rule, with time 297 s vs 131 s. App. D: lower cyclomatic complexity (5.37 -> 3.95) and Halstead volume, maintainability index 78.3 vs 85.1, docstring rate 47% -> 1%. No significance tests

Distinguished methods mainly on length and tokens; PR differences small (often 0.01-0.03 on 100 samples). Repeatability: 10-seed check in one setting only (four methods, gpt-4.1-mini, BCB) (SDs 0.015-0.032 on PR, comparable to differences). Limitations stated: brevity objective may slightly lower PR on complex tasks; stochasticity and bias of LLM mutator/judge; length used as proxy for cost; maintainability and architecture not explored
fields.why: The 10-seed check covers four configurations (methods) in one backbone/benchmark setting, not one configuration

fields.v: Coding rules can be evolved to cut code length and inference cost while keeping correctness. Limitations: possible PR drop on complex tasks; mutator/judge stochasticity and bias; other dimensions (maintainability, architectural complexity) left to future work

Not about SDD (coding rules / AGENTS.md optimisation). Text claims RuleEvolve 'consistently achieves the highest or equal PR across all benchmarks', but Tables 5-6 show lower PR in some cells (e.g. SDK gpt-4.1-mini HE 0.93 vs 0.97 no rule; OpenHands gpt-5.3-codex BCB-H 0.27 vs 0.29; OpenHands Qwen HE 0.96 vs 0.99 manual). Tables 1-2 ('backbone with the highest pass rate') do not use one backbone: Table 1 No rule is the gpt-4.1-mini row, the other Table 1 rows gpt-5.3-codex; Table 2 Prompt-Ops row mixes backbones per benchmark (BCB gpt-4.1-mini, BCB-H gpt-5.3-codex, HE gpt-5-mini), so the text's Prompt-Ops vs RuleEvolve comparison (0.43 vs 0.52) crosses backbones.
